i got my playstation vr today and have played it for a few hours so far. even though i got four games- playstation vr worlds, rigs mechanized combat, battle zone, and rez infinity (it also came with a demo disk)- i've only played vr worlds.

it was pretty easy to hook up and there is even three videos online that show you how to do it if you don't want to read through the very clear instruction booklet. basically the vr processor unit, which is a box roughly 5 1/2" x 5 1/2" x 2", attaches between your tv and the ps4 via hdmi cables. the set i got came with the playstation eye, all the necessary cables, and some pretty good earbuds (but you can use your own or even headphones if you like although headphones might be hard to wear while wearing the vr headset.) it also came with the demo disc and the playstation vr worlds.

the vr headset itself is pretty heavy but is very comfortable with the way it fits on your head. i didn't notice it at all once i started playing. it seemed to track really well too. i didn't notice any lag or blur while playing. the only thing i would say that is kind of negative about it is that it doesn't have super high resolution. everything i played looked a little grainy if i concentrated on it. there was plenty of detail- metal looked like metal, the fish looked real, there were some cool smoke effects, etc. but blacks didn't look perfectly black and even though the graphics were good they weren't up to the level that a non-vr game is at. don't get me wrong, it looked really good but not really great. however, it isn't a deal buster in any way just something i thought i should mention.

for example one of the "games" on the vr worlds was called ocean descent. this is basically a walking simulator where you are in a scuba suit in a dive cage and are lowered to the ocean depths. you don't do anything but look around passively. that being said this is the "game" i would use to demonstrate it to your friends as it is really beautiful and being able to look around in every direction- up and down included- was pretty amazing. there is a tank of compressed air attached to the cage in front of you with a pressure gauge on it. you can see the markings but the grainy quality i mentioned before comes into play and you can't see any individual numbers or letters on it. it's a small thing really and didn't take me out of the experience but i think it's worth mentioning that there will be points where you notice that the resolution isn't perfect. all in all this is a really interesting experience- all the flora and fauna look cool and as i said before looking all around including below and above me was really mind blowing.

another game on the disk is what's called danger ball which is basically vr face pong. instead of going left to right the ball goes away and towards you. you move the paddle around by looking where you want it to be. it's pong, but it was kinda cool. you can put english on the ball by flicking your head as you made contact which was pretty fun to be honest. don't really think there's a lot of depth here obviously but it was fun enough.

i tried vr luge and it was pretty fun, but not really my thing. it's a basic race game where you run a course for several heats to get a total time. the course changes slightly in between heats for variety. there are plenty of obstacles to dodge but i didn't really find it that interesting. i guess if it interested me i could get better at the controls which you use your head for but i was careening all over the place. as i said not really my thing.

then there was scavengers odyssey which is a science fiction tank adventure. this was pretty cool as you did a little bit of running and jumping but also get to shoot a lot of aliens too. it also does a good job of having your perspective switch a lot as you jump on walls and ceilings to get around asteroids and derelict ships as you try to find an alien artifact. you used the regular playstation controller to play this game and it looked really good, but this was the only one of the bunch that i felt a little motion sickness while i played. a couple of caveats- this was the last game i played, my a/c was off so the room was a little hot, and i was pretty tired. it may well be that the very slight queasiness i felt had more to do with these factors than the game and it was very slight anyway. cool game that shows a lot of promise for what the system might do in the future.

the last game on the disk that i played was called the london heist and this was by far the coolest and most fun of the bunch. it reminded me of the old virtua cop series with the added interactivity of vr. i don't want to say too much about this game because i don't want to spoil the enjoyment of discovery so i'll just say there's some shooting and some manipulation of objects in a classic heist story. it was way too short, but so much fun while it lasted. it also has a couple of shooting gallery modes that were pretty fun too. this was also the only game on the vr worlds disk that gave you the option of using the move sticks to play and i would definitely encourage you to play it this way.

all in all i really like the playstation vr. the resolution issue is a small quibble and once you start to play really isn't an issue at all. i am looking forward to playing the other games i bought and i have a very positive view of what it might do once people start making more games and exploring what it can be used for. i highly recommend it to anyone who has a ps4.

feel free to ask me anything you might want to know and i'll do my best to answer!
